notes: Background: mid-market B2B productivity SaaS. Heavy realtime chat + search features for enterprise customers.
Initial engagement: started on hosted API (Jan 2026) to validate latency + quality. Quick POC for chat flows (system + user messages, 8-12 turn sessions).
Hosted findings: avg latency 120-160ms on hosted API (p95 ~340ms). Quality good; token spend higher than expected on open model default prompts.
Reason for Dedicated: predictable unit economics at scale, VPC requirement for several customers, and desire to control model variants + quantization profiles.
POC on Dedicated: 2-week pilot env provisioned (Feb 16-29). Tested 4 vGPU nodes, continuous batching, KV prefix caching. Observed 30-45% cost reduction with caching + batching.
Pricing ask (customer): 12-month committed capacity with 6-month ramp schedule; monthly ramp increments and options for temporary burst above commit for product launches.
Key negotiation points: commit levels (small/medium/large pools), burst credits (hours/day and max tokens), overage rate floor, and ramp schedule with forgiveness windows.

Customer wants: 1) tiered discounts that increase with commit level, 2) explicit burst pool (2x committed capacity for up to 6 hours/day) without immediate overage charge if within monthly burst budget, 3) predictable overage price < list by 15% for first 3 months after commit breach.
Security/Compliance: require SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for customer keys, and EU data residency for a subset of customers (ask: hybrid residency support?).
Operational asks: per-route tracing, token-level cost breakdown in console, and ability to pin model versions during rollout windows.
Internal stakeholders: VP Product (Anya Patel) very cost-sensitive; CTO (Ben Cho) focuses on ops and residency; Head of Security (Rina Bose) needs SOC2 + KMS signoff.

Quote/ballpark they received: Redwood proposal: committed monthly spend $8k / $20k / $50k for small/med/large pools with 15% discount vs hosted list; they countered asking for steeper ramp credits and burst buffer.
Competitive concern: comparing Redwood Dedicated TCO vs OpenAI + custom infra (roughly similar unit compute but Redwood adds orchestration + caching savings).
Stated timeline: procurement asks final pricing in March; wants legal/contract in April. Close target aligned to product launch in June.
Misc crib notes from call: 'need zero surprises on bill — show me the token math', 'burst for launches is non-negotiable', security wants a 30-day data deletion SLA for EU customers.'
